john.doe (AcmeCo): Hey team — running into streaming issues with your /v1/chat/stream endpoint. Clients see partial events then connection drops after ~65s. Happening for multiple users behind our ALB+Cloudflare stack. Request id: req-7f3b21. Example: we get first 2-3 SSE messages then a hard close, no retry headers. This started after a weekend deploy, but might be unrelated. Can you help triage?

alice_support: Thanks John — sorry about the outage. Can you paste an example curl or SDK code that reproduces it and the model/route? Any proxy/nginx/ALB logs around req-7f3b21 would help.

john.doe (AcmeCo): Repro curl below (we're using --no-buffer). Model: gpt-4o-mini-infer.
```
curl -v -H \"Accept: text/event-stream\" \\
  -H \"Authorization: Bearer <REDACTED>\" \\
  -N \"https://api.redwood.example.com/v1/chat/stream?model=gpt-4o-mini-infer\" \\
  --no-buffer
```
We also observe this behavior only from clients routed through Cloudflare; internal tests bypassing CF are stable.

alice_support: Good signal. @ben_infra can you look for any ALB idle timeouts or Cloudflare buffer events for req-7f3b21? Also any Nginx/Envoy proxy config that might be buffer/flush sensitive?

ben_infra: Looking now. Quick notes: ALB default idle timeout = 60s, closes connections with no bytes sent/received. Cloudflare by default will buffer responses to the edge for a bit — streaming SSE can be problematic unless origin sends frequent flushes or we set appropriate headers. Pulling logs...

deploy-bot: deploy event: service=redwood-proxy image=proxy:2025.11.01 sha=abc123 deployed at 2025-11-01T03:12:45Z to prod-us-east-1

claire_runtime: FWIW our runtime flush behavior changed in 2025-10 patch — we switched to coalesced token flushes to reduce CPU; that means if app produces <n tokens in 1s we might buffer before flushing. That could interact badly with proxies expecting heartbeat pinging.

ben_infra: Found ALB connection logs for client IP x.x.x.x and req-7f3b21: ALB closed after 61s with code 504 (idle timeout). Downstream (proxy->runtime) shows no error — runtime kept sending but proxy didn't flush every token. Also see Cloudflare `cf-cache-status: BYPASS` but with `content-length: chunked` — CF sometimes buffers until a flush or full chunk.

john.doe (AcmeCo): We see the same symptom across users — first payloads arrive, then blank, then connection resets at ~65s. If we add keepalive pings every 20s it looks stable. Our mobile SDK can't easily add pings so we need a server-side fix.

alice_support: Thanks — sounds like interaction between coalesced flushes and intermediary timeouts/buffering. Two parallel mitigation paths: 1) origin-side: ensure the streaming response emits small heartbeat comments/newlines frequently (SSE canonical `:\n\n`) or lower the flush threshold in runtime, 2) edge-side: bump ALB idle timeout (e.g., to 120s) or configure Cloudflare to use `Origin Stream`/disable buffering for that route. Can we try origin heartbeat as quick repro?

claire_runtime: I can roll a hotfix toggle to reduce coalescing and emit an SSE-style comment every 15s while the customer request is active. Patch will be small. Suggest doing that as a temporary mitigation while infra investigates ALB/CF settings.

ben_infra: Also a note for nginx/Envoy: in nginx use `proxy_buffering off; proxy_send_timeout 300s; proxy_read_timeout 300s;` and ensure `X-Accel-Buffering: no` is forwarded to upstream. Envoy needs `stream_idle_timeout` and `connection_idletimeout` tuned. ALB needs `idle_timeout.timeout_seconds` increased.

john.doe (AcmeCo): That would be great. If you can emit heartbeats from the origin that might be the fastest fix. Any chance Cloudflare is dropping HTTP/2->1.1 translation? We saw some differences when clients used HTTP/2.

ben_infra: CF sometimes terminates HTTP/2 at edge and speaks HTTP/1.1 to origin; that shouldn't break streaming but buffering semantics can change. Also if `Content-Encoding: gzip` gets applied at edge that will force buffering until stream ends. Confirming response headers for req-7f3b21 show no gzip.

claire_runtime: Hotfix pushed to staging: `runtime.flush_interval_ms = 15000; runtime.sse_comment_heartbeat = true` — rolling to prod in 2m for requests tagged with `experimental-heartbeat` route. Will scope to affected customers first.

alice_support: John — can you whitelist your account ID so we route your traffic to the experimental heartbeat route? Then try reproducing without client-side pings.

john.doe (AcmeCo): Whitelisted. Re-testing now...

john.doe (AcmeCo): Good news: with heartbeat enabled I get continuous events, no drop at 65s. Looks stable on our end for 10m test.

ben_infra: Confirmed in ALB access logs: with heartbeat we see periodic bytes so ALB keeps connection open. No 504s for the new reqs. Cloudflare logs show streaming passthrough with no additional buffering triggered.

alice_support: Excellent. Next steps: 1) Claire / runtime to make heartbeat opt-in flag available for more customers + telemetry, 2) Infra to review ALB idle timeout at account level and document recommended config for SSE streaming (we recommend >=120s), 3) Docs/KB with nginx/Envoy headers (`X-Accel-Buffering: no`, `Transfer-Encoding: chunked`, `proxy_buffering off`), 4) Engineering follow-up to adjust coalescing heuristics long-term.

claire_runtime: I'll open an RFC to change default flush heuristics and add an opt-in runtime header `X-Redwood-Stream-Heartbeat: 15s`. Also will add a metric emit when flushes are suppressed so we can correlate customer drops.

dana_oncall: Logging action: mark incident P2, owner=eng-runtime, sla impact: partial streaming degradation for customers behind buffering proxies. Add timeline to postmortem after we finish root cause analysis.

john.doe (AcmeCo): Thanks everyone — heartbeat hotfix works for us. Please keep me posted on the permanent fix and any recommended edge config. Appreciate quick turnaround. :heart: 

alice_support: Thanks John — closing this support thread but we will follow up in a postmortem and update KB. If you see any regressions ping this thread. :thumbsup:
